scope: Focused minimum-billing implementation research; no article/source edits
conclusion: Verified: §25.194 is adopted/effective and requires SLLIA acknowledgment of minimum billing under §25.193. Verified: the Project 58000 large-load minimum-billing treatment in the July 24 Texas Register is proposed. No later adopted §25.193 body or effective date was verified. Treat numerical/duration/start-of-billing terms as proposed, and the October 13 current status as pending/not verified adopted rather than claiming an operative charge.
currentStatusConfidence: Primary bodies establish proposal versus cross-reference distinction; exhaustive October 13 docket/current-code verification unavailable because official current endpoints blocked access.

primaryEvidence.pinpoint: Introductory proposal; Project 58000 comments and questions; proposed §25.193(d)(2)-(3); filing TRD-202602812
primaryEvidence.details: Proposes greatest-of contracted peak/prior-year NCP/12CP minimum demand, commencement at available service irrespective of energization or full utilization, and no less than 20 years. Filed July 9; earliest possible adoption August 23 is not adoption/effective date.

Proposes at-least-20-year agreement, billing first cycle after capacity available, 240 consecutive payments, and tariff compliance filing within 30 days of adoption. These proposed tariff provisions are not proof of utility implementation.

primaryEvidence.pinpoint: Minimum transmission/minimum demand charge Commission Response (51 TexReg 6879); §25.194(f)(2)(B)(ii), (f)(2)(D), (f)(3)(A)(iii)(V), (f)(3)(C); effective-date notice
primaryEvidence.details: Commission expressly assigns charge details to Project 58000; operative §25.194 requires acknowledgment, allows related additional security, includes billing obligation among outstanding amounts, and links staged security return to agreement milestones. It supplies no charge amount or duration itself.

materialConflicts: Adopted §25.194 cross-references §25.193 while its response explicitly defers charge details to Project 58000. Do not convert that reference into adoption of the July proposal.
Secondary summaries sometimes describe Commission approval without distinguishing proposal-for-publication from adoption. No such summary overrides the official Proposed Rules label.
July proposed §25.193 says no less than 20 years while proposed §25.252 specifies first 20 years/240 payments. Both remain proposal terms; avoid choosing a final duration from them.

blockedPrimaryChecks.result: September 22 implementation-roadmap lead discovered through linked secondary source; actual primary body 403, so its claimed December schedule is not adopted as evidence

supportedReaderImplication: The adopted interconnection rule makes minimum billing and related security part of diligence, but a business cannot price a recurring bill, minimum-demand duration, or security-release calendar from §25.194 alone. Obtain the final applicable §25.193 treatment, approved tariff, and actual SLLIA terms before modeling a ramp or exit.
recommendedArticleQualification: The adopted SLLIA provisions anticipate minimum billing under §25.193; the July transmission-cost-recovery proposal supplies proposed terms, not a verified effective minimum charge or duration. Keep actual billing and collateral release subject to the applicable final rule, tariff and agreement.
nextVerification: Inspect complete Project 58000 docket through October 13 and latest official §25.193/current-code history; retrieve any adoption order and TexReg effective-date notice. Verify utility tariff/SLLIA separately; do not infer private terms.
